definitions.explanation: The maximum speed at which vehicles are legally permitted to travel on a road. Set by traffic regulations and indicated by road signs.

examples.japanese: {制限速度|せいげんそくど}を{守|まも}ってください。
この{道路|どうろ}の{制限速度|せいげんそくど}は{時速|じそく}60キロだ。
examples.english: The speed limit on this road is 60 km/h.

examples.japanese: {制限速度|せいげんそくど}を{超|こ}えて{走|はし}ると、{罰金|ばっきん}を{取|と}られる。
examples.english: If you drive over the speed limit, you'll be fined.

examples.japanese: {住宅街|じゅうたくがい}では{制限速度|せいげんそくど}が{時速|じそく}30キロに{引|ひ}き{下|さ}げられた。
examples.english: The speed limit was reduced to 30 km/h in residential areas.

notes:
Essential vocabulary for driving in Japan. Japan's standard speed limits are 60 km/h on general roads and 100 km/h on expressways, though many residential and school zones have lower limits. Compound of 制限 (limit, restriction) + 速度 (speed).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {制限速度|せいげんそくど}を{守|まも}る: to obey the speed limit
- {制限速度|せいげんそくど}を{超|こ}える: to exceed the speed limit
- {制限速度|せいげんそくど}{違反|いはん}: speed limit violation
- {制限速度|せいげんそくど}の{標識|ひょうしき}: speed limit sign
- {制限速度|せいげんそくど}を{引|ひ}き{下|さ}げる: to lower the speed limit

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {速度制限|そくどせいげん}: speed restriction — same meaning, different word order; used more broadly
- {最高速度|さいこうそくど}: maximum speed — can refer to a vehicle's top speed or to the legal limit
